insight.title: Why Reacting Faster Actually Slows You Down
insight.subtitle: How a three-second delay protects your best decisions

sections.text: Every app you own is designed to make you react instantly. But as automation handles the "doing," your only leverage is "thinking." The faster you respond, the less you actually contribute to the result.

Speed often hides shallow logic. When you remove the gap between a prompt and your reaction, you aren't deciding; you are simply processing. Real power lies in the deliberate pause that breaks the cycle.
In tomorrow’s economy, being fast is a commodity. Being right is a premium. A five-second delay in a high-stakes email or meeting allows your intuition to catch up with your reflexes.
Try this today: When you receive a digital notification today, count to five before you touch your device.
Intelligence is the distance you create between a stimulus and your response.
